newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., stadium may seek loan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., stadium may seek loan - paper.

text.p: The Tampa Sports Authority may ask the city or Hillsborough County to back up to $20 million of loans to keep football stadium construction on schedule until a bond financing dispute is resolved, the Tampa Tribune said Tuesday.
A pending lawsuit by former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe has forced the authority to delay the issue of $158 million of revenue bonds that were to finance the facility.

Poe's suit claims that the bonds, which would be repaid partly from sales taxes, would illegally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Depositions began Tuesday in the lawsuit.
Construction began last fall. Without the bond sale, the authority will run out of construction money in late April, interim director Henry Saavedra told the newspaper.

The stadium is scheduled to be finished in time for the start of the 1998 football season. The authority must pay the team a penalty of $437,500 for each game that must be played elsewhere if the new stadium is unfinished by then.

In the meantime, the city and county are seeking validation of the bonds in a hearing set for March 3 in Hillsborough County Circuit Court. The ruling will automatically be appealed to the Florida Supreme Court.
